q.t: Find the error: She go to school by bus.
q.e: She (singular) in the simple present → goes.

q.t: Find the error: I saw a elephant at the zoo.
q.e: ‘elephant’ starts with a vowel sound → an.

q.t: Find the error: Yesterday we play cricket.
q.e: ‘Yesterday’ is past → played.

q.t: Find the error: The children is playing.
q.e: ‘children’ is plural → are.

q.t: Find the error: He can swims very well.
q.e: After a modal, use V1: can swim.

q.t: Find the missing word: She is fond ___ music.
q.e: The fixed pair is ‘fond of’.

q.t: Find the missing word: I want ___ become a doctor.
q.e: ‘want’ is followed by to + V1.

q.t: Find the error: Me and Riya went home.
q.e: It's the subject → I. Politely, put yourself last: Riya and I.

q.t: Find the error: She sings very good.
q.e: Describes how she sings → adverb: well.

q.t: Find the missing word: He reached school ___ 8 o'clock.
q.e: Clock time → at.

q.t: Find the error: One of my friends live in Pune.
q.e: The subject is ‘One’ → lives.

q.t: Find the error: I have went there twice.
q.e: After ‘have’, use V3: gone.

q.t: Find the error: She is good in mathematics.
q.e: The fixed pair is ‘good at’.

q.t: Find the error: He did not came yesterday.
q.e: ‘did’ carries the past, so use V1: come.

q.t: Find the error: This is the boy which won the prize.
q.e: For a person → who.

q.t: Find the missing word: There ___ many people at the fair.
q.e: The real subject ‘many people’ is plural → were (past).

q.t: Find the missing word: He is ___ best player in our team.
q.e: Superlatives take ‘the’.

q.t: Find the error: She is more taller than her sister.
q.e: Don't use ‘more’ with -er.

q.t: Find the error: We discussed about the plan.
q.e: ‘discuss’ takes no preposition.

q.t: Find the error: Each of the students have a book.
q.e: ‘Each’ is singular → has.

q.t: Find the error: If it will rain, we will stay home.
q.e: After ‘if’ for a future idea, use the simple present.

q.t: Find the error: I am knowing the answer.
q.e: ‘know’ is a stative verb — no continuous form.

q.t: Find the error: The news are very shocking.
q.e: ‘news’ is singular.

q.t: Find the error: He has been working here since five years.
q.e: ‘five years’ is a length of time → for.

q.t: Find the error: I have seen him last week.
q.e: ‘last week’ is a finished time → simple past.

q.t: Find the missing word: The train had left ___ we reached the station.
q.e: The train left first (past perfect), then we reached → before.

q.t: Find the missing word: She asked me ___ I was ready.
q.e: A reported yes/no question → if/whether.

q.t: Find the error: Neither Ravi nor his friends was there.
q.e: Agree with the nearer subject ‘friends’ → were.

q.t: Find the error: The letter was wrote by Meena.
q.e: Passive needs V3: written.

q.t: Find the error: Although he was poor, but he was honest.
q.e: ‘Although’ already shows contrast.

q.t: Editing — find the error in this line: Last summer my family visit Shimla for a week.
q.e: ‘Last summer’ sets the past → visited.

q.t: Next line: We stayed in a hotel who was near the Mall Road.
q.e: A hotel is a thing → which (or that).

q.t: Next line: Every morning we walks up to the ridge.
q.e: We (plural) and the story is in the past → walked.

q.t: Next line: The view of the mountains were breathtaking.
q.e: The subject is ‘view’ (singular); ‘of the mountains’ only describes it.

q.t: Omission — choose the missing word: On the last day, we bought gifts ___ our friends.
q.e: Gifts intended for someone → for.

q.t: Find the error: Hardly had I reached the station than the train left.
q.e: ‘Hardly’ pairs with ‘when’; ‘No sooner’ pairs with ‘than’.

q.t: Find the error: He told that he was busy.
q.e: ‘told’ needs a person (told me); otherwise use ‘said’.

q.t: Find the error: The number of students are increasing.
q.e: ‘The number of’ is one figure → singular.

q.t: Gap-fill with the right tense: By the time the doctor came, the patient ___. (die)
q.e: The death came before the doctor's arrival — earlier of two past actions → past perfect.

q.t: Find the error: Walking along the beach, a big wave knocked me down.
o: The participle dangles — the wave wasn't walking
q.e: The phrase must belong to the subject: Walking along the beach, I was knocked down by a big wave.
